milestones.title: Functional validator drives the app in live QA mode

features.title: Grant functional validator its configured tools (allow-list) + mock-seam integration test
features.spec:
Background: Kranz spawns headless `claude -p` sessions. A SessionSpec has three tool fields: `tools` (emitted as `--tools`, the EXCLUSIVE built-in tool set — which tools EXIST), `allowed_tools` (`--allowedTools`, auto-approved calls), `disallowed_tools` (`--disallowedTools`, denied; deny wins over allow). In `-p` mode there are NO interactive prompts: a tool call that exists but is not auto-approved FAILS (see docs/design.md lines 32-33).

The prerequisite scrutiny-floor mission already wired per-role config `tools` -> SessionSpec.tools -> `--tools`. Confirm by reading, and follow the existing style exactly: crates/engine/src/runner.rs `run_validator` sets `tools: cfg.role(kind).tools.clone()` (~line 767); crates/engine/src/permissions.rs `apply()` deliberately does NOT touch spec.tools (see its doc comment ~line 169); crates/engine/src/backend_claude.rs emits `--tools` when spec.tools is non-empty (~line 324). So a functional validator already RECEIVES its configured tools in `--tools`.

Gap to close: those configured tools are only in the exclusive set, not auto-approved, so a browser/computer-use tool would FAIL headless. Fix: for the FUNCTIONAL validator ONLY (never scrutiny), fold its configured EXTRA tools into `allowed_tools` so they are auto-approved, while keeping the read-only deny list intact.

Implementation in crates/engine/src/permissions.rs `for_role`: the `Role::ValidatorScrutiny | Role::ValidatorFunctional` arm builds `allowed` from Read/Glob/Grep + git-inspect + contract-command patterns. AFTER that, ONLY when `role == Role::ValidatorFunctional`, append each configured tool name from `cfg.validator_functional.tools` to `allowed`, EXCLUDING the standard inspect tools in the `INSPECT_TOOLS` constant (Bash, Read, Glob, Grep). This exclusion is critical: those inspect tools are already governed by precise existing allow patterns, and adding a bare `Bash` entry would broaden Bash to ALL commands and break the read-only guarantee. Then call `dedup_preserving_order`. Do NOT change the scrutiny code path. Keep `disallowed_tools = READ_ONLY_DENY` and `permission_mode = "default"` unchanged. Do not alter `profile.tools`. `for_role` already takes `&MissionConfig`, so `cfg.validator_functional.tools` is available.

Also update the docs/design.md section-4.7 permission table (or a footnote beneath it): note that the functional validator ADDITIONALLY auto-approves any EXTRA tools listed in `validatorFunctional.tools` (e.g. a browser tool) to enable live-QA mode, while Write/Edit/WebFetch/WebSearch/git-push remain denied. Keep this edit minimal.

Integration test: add to crates/engine/tests/backend_mock_test.rs, mirroring the existing `worker_session_carries_configured_tools_onto_the_spec` test and reusing its mock-backend spec-capture harness (read it first; do NOT invent a new harness). Name the new test EXACTLY `functional_validator_tools_are_carried_and_allowed`. Build a MissionConfig where `validator_functional.tools = vec!["Bash".into(), "Read".into(), "Glob".into(), "Grep".into(), "FakeBrowserTool".into()]` — use the clearly-fake placeholder `FakeBrowserTool`; do NOT assume any real installed tool name. Drive the functional-validator spawn through the same seam the worker test uses (run_validator with the mock backend) and capture the SessionSpec. Assert ALL of: (1) spec.tools equals the configured list verbatim; (2) spec.allowed_tools contains "FakeBrowserTool"; (3) spec.allowed_tools does NOT contain a bare "Bash" entry; (4) spec.disallowed_tools still contains "Write" and "Edit". Additionally assert (in this test or a sibling) that a SCRUTINY validator built with the same configured tools does NOT get "FakeBrowserTool" folded into its allowed_tools (live-QA is functional-only).

Ensure `cargo test -p kranz-engine` is green and `cargo clippy -p kranz-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. Touch ONLY: crates/engine/src/permissions.rs, crates/engine/tests/backend_mock_test.rs, docs/design.md (and crates/engine/src/runner.rs ONLY if the spawn seam genuinely requires it — prefer permissions.rs alone).
validationCriteria: A functional validator whose config `tools` includes a non-inspect tool ('FakeBrowserTool') produces a SessionSpec whose `allowed_tools` contains that tool name.
The same SessionSpec's `tools` field equals the configured list verbatim, and `disallowed_tools` still contains 'Write' and 'Edit'.
Folding configured tools into `allowed_tools` never adds a bare 'Bash' entry (Bash stays restricted to the existing precise patterns).
A scrutiny validator built with the same configured tools does NOT get the extra non-inspect tool folded into its `allowed_tools`.

A test named exactly `functional_validator_tools_are_carried_and_allowed` exists in crates/engine/tests/backend_mock_test.rs and passes, `cargo test -p kranz-engine` is green, and `cargo clippy -p kranz-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

features.title: Add always-on Live QA section to the functional validator prompt
features.spec:
File: crates/engine/prompts/validator-functional.md. Read it fully first. It is the append-system-prompt for the functional validator, rendered UNCONDITIONALLY by the runner (no per-mission templating of this section is required). The role currently verifies a milestone by running contract commands and reading output, and ends with a strict findings-JSON message.

Add a new section whose heading includes the words "Live QA". The section must be ALWAYS present in the file but SELF-ACTIVATE only when the session actually has browser/computer-use tools available (activated by tool presence, NOT by a template flag or engine variable). When such tools are available (i.e. beyond the standard Bash/Read/Glob/Grep), it must instruct the validator to:
- Recognize it is in 'live QA mode' and DRIVE THE BUILT APPLICATION rather than judge behaviour from command output alone.
- Start the app per the repository's own run/dev docs (e.g. README or docs) — do not assume a fixed command.
- Exercise EACH acceptance criterion / contract assertion behaviourally against the running app.
- Capture concrete evidence in the report: URLs visited, exact observed on-screen text/state, and screenshots if the tooling supports them.
- Fall back to command/read evidence for any criterion that cannot be exercised live, and say so explicitly.
- Stay READ-ONLY: drive the app, never edit its source or commit.

Constraints: Do NOT hardcode any specific tool name — the installed claude's browser/computer tooling varies and the config carries the list; refer to 'browser/computer-use tools' generically. Keep the change ADDITIVE: do not weaken existing instructions, and do NOT change the final findings-JSON contract or the read-only boundaries already stated. Live-QA evidence must flow into the SAME findings/summary JSON the role already emits.

Touch ONLY crates/engine/prompts/validator-functional.md. If (and only if) `cargo test -p kranz-engine` has a test that pins this prompt's content or hash and it fails because of your edit, update that test's expected value; do not otherwise touch tests.
validationCriteria: crates/engine/prompts/validator-functional.md contains an always-present section (heading including 'Live QA') that instructs the validator to drive the built application when browser/computer-use tools are available.

The section activates on tool presence (no template flag/variable), tells the validator to start the app per repo docs, exercise each acceptance criterion live, and capture evidence (URLs visited, observed text/state).
The section does not hardcode any specific tool name and refers to browser/computer-use tools generically.
The change is additive: the existing findings-JSON contract and read-only boundaries remain intact, and `cargo test -p kranz-engine` stays green.

features.title: Write docs/validating-uis.md cookbook with config block and dashboard worked example
features.spec:
Create a new file docs/validating-uis.md — a cookbook for putting the functional validator into 'live QA mode' so it drives a running UI instead of judging from code. Touch ONLY docs/validating-uis.md (no code, no other docs).

Cover, concretely:
1. The convention: adding browser/computer-use tooling to the functional validator's config turns it into live-QA mode; the prompt (crates/engine/prompts/validator-functional.md) already teaches the behaviour and self-activates on tool presence.
2. A concrete `.kranz/config.json` block. Config is layered (compiled defaults < ~/.kranz/config.json < <repo>/.kranz/config.json; later wins), keys are camelCase, and files may be partial. Show setting `validatorFunctional.tools`. CALL OUT PROMINENTLY: `tools` is the EXCLUSIVE `--tools` set — it REPLACES the default tool set for that role — so you MUST list the inspection tools the validator still needs (`Bash`, `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`) ALONGSIDE the browser tool, or the validator loses the ability to run its contract commands. Use a clearly-marked PLACEHOLDER for the browser tool name (e.g. `"<your-installed-browser-tool>"`) and explain the exact name is whatever the installed `claude` exposes — do NOT hardcode a real name. Example shape: {"validatorFunctional": {"tools": ["Bash","Read","Glob","Grep","<your-installed-browser-tool>"]}}
3. A brief permission-model note: the engine auto-approves the functional validator's configured EXTRA tools (so the browser tool actually runs in headless `-p` mode) while Write/Edit/WebFetch/WebSearch/git-push stay denied — the validator drives the app but cannot modify it. (Implemented in crates/engine/src/permissions.rs.)
4. A WORKED EXAMPLE against this repo's own dashboard (apps/dashboard). READ apps/dashboard/README.md and apps/dashboard/package.json scripts to get the REAL start/dev command. Show: how the validator starts the dashboard, one or two concrete acceptance-style criteria driven live (e.g. navigate to the local dev URL, observe a specific UI element/text that proves a milestone behaviour), and exactly what evidence to record (URL visited, observed text). Keep every command accurate to what apps/dashboard actually provides.
5. A short 'evidence in the report' note: live observations flow into the functional validator's normal findings/summary JSON.

Keep it a focused cookbook (about one to two screens).
validationCriteria: docs/validating-uis.md exists and contains a `.kranz/config.json` example that sets `validatorFunctional.tools`.
The config example lists Bash, Read, Glob, and Grep alongside a placeholder browser tool, and the doc explicitly warns that `tools` is the exclusive set so the inspection tools must be included.
The doc does not hardcode a real browser/computer-use tool name (uses a placeholder) and states the name depends on the installed claude.
The doc includes a worked apps/dashboard example with a start command accurate to apps/dashboard and at least one live-driven acceptance criterion plus the evidence to capture.
The doc explains that the functional validator's configured extra tools are auto-approved while Write/Edit remain denied.
